facts.text: The name "Echo Park" in West Hempstead is an acronym created from the first four local Little League baseball teams in the area: Eagles, Cardinals, Hawks, and Orioles.
Three train stops serve the area—West Hempstead, Hempstead Gardens, and Lakeview—linking residents to the broader Long Island network.
West Hempstead got its name when the Long Island Rail Road built a station on Hempstead Turnpike in 1891, turning “West of Hempstead” into the town’s official title.
The West Hempstead Public Library began in a storefront in 1956, earned a state charter in 1967, and moved into its 28,000‑square‑foot building in 2007.
Riesterer’s Bakery, founded in 1931, still serves kosher pastries along Hempstead Avenue, a staple of the neighborhood’s culinary scene.
The app you're using, Town Crier, was built right here in West Hempstead in 2026!
